Graphics & UI

Terminal user interfaces with Ose

Ose: The Odù of Expression

Ose governs visual expression — terminal UI, rendering, and layout. Feature-gated behind game. Uses ratatui for terminal manipulation.

Initializing the Terminal

Init & Restore 
// Initialize terminal (alternate screen, raw mode)
Ose.bere();

// ... draw UI ...

// Restore terminal to normal mode
Ose.pari();
// Initialize terminal (alternate screen, raw mode)
Ose.init();

// ... draw UI ...

// Restore terminal to normal mode
Ose.end();

Drawing

Draw 
// Draw a widget map to the screen
Ose.ya(widgets);

// Print at a specific position
Ose.ko_si(10, 5, "Hello at position");

Layout

Layout

Mini App

Counter App 
isodale counter_app() {
    Ose.bere();
    defer {
        Ose.pari();  // cleanup on exit
    }
    
    ayanmo count = 0;
    ayanmo running = otito;
    
    nigba (running) {
        // Draw
        Ose.ya({ "text": "Count: " + count });
        
        // Handle input
        ayanmo key = Ose.gbile();
        yan (key) {
            "q" => { running = iro; }
            "+" => { count = count + 1; }
            "-" => { count = count - 1; }
        }
    }
}

counter_app();
fn counter_app() {
    Ose.init();
    defer {
        Ose.end();  // cleanup on exit
    }
    
    let count = 0;
    let running = true;
    
    while (running) {
        // Draw
        Ose.draw({ "text": "Count: " + count });
        
        // Handle input
        let key = Ose.read_key();
        match (key) {
            "q" => { running = false; }
            "+" => { count = count + 1; }
            "-" => { count = count - 1; }
        }
    }
}

counter_app();
Feature Gate

The Ose domain requires tui feature flag in your Ifa.toml: [features] game = ["ifa-std/game"]
